title: ALERTCalifornia AI camera alert sends Cal Fire engines to a night fire near Auburn before any 911 call
summary: AI camera alert at 2:33 a.m. on 6 July 2024 sent Cal Fire engines to a fire near Auburn before any 911 call; held to a 30 x 30 ft area
account: The ALERTCalifornia camera network, operated by UC San Diego with AI smoke-detection software from DigitalPath of Chico, California, and used by Cal Fire, posted an alert at 2:33 a.m. on July 6 of a fire near Auburn, in the foothills east of Sacramento; the report, published in September 2025, gives the day but not the year, and places the case among the previous year's fires, so 2024 is used. Nobody had called 911. Cal Fire's Grass Valley Emergency Command Center verified the alert and sent engines, and crews put the fire out before it spread beyond a 30 x 30 foot area. Cal Fire Deputy Chief Brian York said that in 2024 the cameras picked up 1,668 of the 7,553 fires in Cal Fire's jurisdiction, 636 of them before any person called 911.
purpose: Built to detect smoke in camera feeds and alert fire dispatchers automatically; this benefit is that purpose.
system: ALERTCalifornia camera network with DigitalPath AI smoke detection
developer: DigitalPath (AI smoke detection); ALERTCalifornia, University of California San Diego (camera network)
deployer: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (Cal Fire)
taxonomy_note: The benefit is prevention of fire spread (wildland, property, life); none of the six types names harm prevention. Environmental sustainability chosen because the protected asset is wildland.

ratings.reason: Cal Fire's Grass Valley command center dispatched engines on the alert and crews extinguished the fire at a 30 x 30 ft area, avoiding a larger night-time incident.
Residents near Auburn benefited from a fire being put out before it spread; the damage avoided is not quantified for this fire in the sources.

ai_role.statement: The AI alert was the only report of the Auburn fire; Cal Fire's command center verified it and dispatched on it. The same source says the system still produces false positives from dust and clouds, so human verification sits between alert and dispatch.

La Panza Ranch, San Luis Obispo County, California; ALERTCalifornia AI notified Cal Fire of smoke with no public 911 call; fire held to about 16 acres (KSBY; Paso Robles Daily News, 29 Oct 2024)
